drivingQuestion: Do exposed buttocks count as nakedness, such that one may not recite Shema or a blessing in their presence?
outcomeNote: The attempt to prove Rav Huna's rule from the mishna of ḥalla is knocked down by Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak's reading; the support from the baraita itself is left standing.

segments.he: אָמַר מָר: זֶה מַחֲזִיר פָּנָיו וְקוֹרֵא קְרִיאַת שְׁמַע. וְהָא אִיכָּא עֲגָבוֹת! מְסַיַּיע לֵיהּ לְרַב הוּנָא, דְּאָמַר רַב הוּנָא: עֲגָבוֹת אֵין בָּהֶם מִשּׁוּם עֶרְוָה. לֵימָא מְסַיַּיע לֵיהּ לְרַב הוּנָא: הָאִשָּׁה יוֹשֶׁבֶת, וְקוֹצָה לָהּ חַלָּתָהּ עֲרוּמָּה, מִפְּנֵי שֶׁיְּכוֹלָה לְכַסּוֹת פָּנֶיהָ בְּקַרְקַע, אֲבָל לֹא הָאִישׁ.
segments.en: The Gemara reverts to clarify something mentioned above. «The Master said» in a baraita: «This» one «turns his head» aside «and recites Shema.» The Gemara notes a difficulty: «Aren’t there» bare «buttocks?» This «supports» the opinion of «Rav Huna, as Rav Huna said: Buttocks do not constitute nakedness. Let us say» that the following mishna «supports Rav Huna’s» opinion: «A woman sits and separates her ḥalla naked,» despite the fact that she must recite a blessing over the separation of the ḥalla, «because she can cover her face,» a euphemism for her genitals, «in the ground, but a male,» whose genitals are not covered when he sits, may «not» do so. The mishna teaches that exposed buttocks do not constitute nakedness.

segments.he: תַּרְגְּמַהּ רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק: כְּגוֹן שֶׁהָיוּ פָּנֶיהָ טוּחוֹת בַּקַּרְקַע.
segments.en: «Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak interpreted» the mishna as referring to «a case where her face,» genitals, «was completely covered in the ground» such that her posterior was covered by the ground. Therefore, proof for Rav Huna’s opinion cannot be brought from this mishna.
